77697.subject: Solana Beats the Bell
77697.body:
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/eaa70932-7ce4-467e-b338-a662ed575d6a/0xR_NL_Banner_Heading_Wordmark.jpg?t=1776775276)
Caption: 

Today we examine whether tokenized stocks on Solana trade at fair prices, measuring Backpack’s fills against each stock’s live quote as an execution desk would. Seven weeks in, larger trades are already competitive with TradFi, while Solana gains an edge after hours. Yesterday brought a broad risk-off move led by a 5% semiconductor unwind, with crypto’s AI complex and miners hit hardest.

———————————————————————————

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/42e942ec-f31d-4957-8722-a3ac7b121e1e/0xR_NL_Market_Update.png?t=1767631151) [Market Update]
Caption: 

Yesterday saw a broad risk-off led by the AI complex. Bittensor Eco (-5.5%) and Crypto Miners (-5.1%) were the worst sectors, followed by L2 (-3.7%) and AI (-2.7%), while Launchpad (2.2%) was the only sector meaningfully green. Gold (-2.2%) and the NASDAQ 100 (-1.9%) fell alongside crypto.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/7cd4dc72-9642-4dfe-8244-40b7b2bf529f/image.png?t=1787143048)
Caption: 

The driver was a semiconductor unwind rather than anything crypto-specific. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index closed down 5.0%, with memory hit hardest as Micron fell 7.0% and SK Hynix's ADRs dropped 9.2%. Reported drivers included elevated Treasury yields and questions about how the AI buildout is being financed. Crypto's AI-linked sectors traded as high-beta expressions of that move.

The weekly picture is more specific. Crypto Miners fell 9.1%, second worst behind DEXs, while BTC gained 1.7%. The decline was concentrated in HUT (-12.5%), CIFR (-11.9%), CORZ (-9.9%), WULF (-9.4%), and RIOT (-7.9%).

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/f75d840d-91c2-4aa9-93a8-ac7de1807c69/image.png?t=1787143048)
Caption: 

Four of those five are the index's YTD leaders, with HUT up 57.6%, RIOT 33.6%, WULF 22.6%, and CORZ 17.9%, while every name that outperformed on the week is flat or negative on the year. The selling sits where the gains are. CIFR is the exception at -0.7% YTD, which points to something beyond profit-taking. 

Financing is the likeliest candidate. An AI data center under construction can cost [$20B before equipment is installed](https://www.swissre.com/institute/research/sigma-research/sigma-insights-07-2026-insuring-ai-data-centre-risks.html), and lenders want all of that value covered, but [insurers will not write that much](https://www.insurancebusinessmag.com/us/news/property/the-coverage-ceiling-arrives-for-hyperscale-data-centers-579429.aspx) on a single site. 77696.subject: SpaceX’s Cursor just killed GitHub
77696.body:
The Atlas

Автор: GenAI Works


Автор: GenAI Works

    
    
    Прочитайте цю статтю на LinkedIn, щоб приєднатися до обговорення
Прочитати на LinkedIn
https://www.linkedin.com/comm/pulse/spacexs-cursor-just-killed-github-genai-works-jl0ef?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_series_follow_newsletter_02%3BPM3P8h7SSZmoxDXxzrgeAg%3D%3D&midToken=AQFTjFOONAfT2w&midSig=3PPHb-SeGIvIo1&trk=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_&trkEmail=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_-null-fz96fz~mt04eug9~mc-null-null&eid=fz96fz-mt04eug9-mc
  
Welcome back! Today: Cursor launching a GitHub rival mid-outage, how few parameters a finetune really needs, 8.3 billion synthetic people and a proof that took 16 hours.  In today's Atlas Newsletter: Who launches a GitHub competitor while GitHub is down? Cursor shipped Origin four days after SpaceX closed its $60 billion acquisition, and the timing wrote its own jokes. How few parameters can you get away with? Full fine tuning a 70B model touches 70 billion. LoRA touches 910 million. One method gets it down to 13. Would you answer the same way? Harvard and MIT built 8.3 billion synthetic personas, and the same simulated people swing 71 points depending on which model voices them. Can a neurosurgeon beat 22 years of mathematics? Shanmu Jin proved Crouzeix's Conjecture with a 16-hour autonomous run and a self-taught math background. PS: Want to collaborate with the biggest GTM engine and distribution moat for AI companies? You can feature your tool with us and reach millions. SpaceXAI's Cursor launched a GitHub rival  Cursor announced Origin, a code hosting platform built into the editor, live in beta for paid users.  GitHub was down at the time. Cursor's Matt Palmer posted the line that turned it into a meme: "We were going to ship this earlier, but GitHub was down."  The team says the timing wasn't planned. Paid users can host repos, manage pull requests without opening a browser, browse and search code where they're already prompting, and sync in real time with GitHub as the source of truth. Cursor's agents can update branches directly inside Origin. The integration list says more than the feature list.  Vercel for deployments, Buildkite and Depot for CI.  Origin is angling to sit at the center of the toolchain teams already wire around GitHub. The awkward part: onboarding starts by importing your GitHub repos. Asked whether you self-host Origin on Origin, Palmer conceded that importing from GitHub is non-optimal when GitHub is down. The structural story is bigger.  Four days earlier, SpaceX closed its $60 billion acquisition of Cursor, folding it into the SpaceXAI team behind Grok 4.6 and Grok Build.  Origin is the first major product since, and it's a direct swing at GitHub's core business. The resulting map is strange.  GitHub belongs to Microsoft, which backs OpenAI. Cursor now sits under SpaceX, which owns Grok. A code host aimed at an OpenAI backer's

77664.subject: Online check-in for a smooth take-off. ATTENTION! Don’t forget – it opens 24 hours before departure. (Y9SB5U)
77664.body:
Hello, Oleh Novosadov!

Your adventure is just around the corner – you’ll soon be boarding your Ryanair flight! There’s just one small step left to ensure a smooth start: online check-in.

It’s easy – do it via the Ryanair app. This way, you avoid unnecessary fees at the airport..

How to do it? Here’s a quick guide:

You will need:
- Booking code: Y9SB5U
- Booking email: novosadov@boarding.sk (it may differ from your personal email address)

If you’re using the Ryanair mobile app, you can check in directly there – it’s fast, convenient and eco-friendly.

When is check-in available?
- From 24 to 2 hours before departure
- If you’ve purchased seats, you can check in as early as 60 days before your flight

Download your boarding passes.

Save them in the app – you’ll need them when going through airport security. Before your trip, make sure your BOARDING PASSES (tickets) are in ELECTRONIC FORM. Download them to your phone.

You’ll find a full step-by-step guide with screenshots in our manual for checking in online via the Ryanair app.

ATTENTION! If you leave the check-in until the airport, it may cost you up to €55.

That’s a lot of money you could use for your next Pelikan adventure instead! Check our calendar of promotional flights and start planning your next trip right now!
